canonical_definition: Helpfulness is the ability of an AI system to produce responses that provide useful, practical, and actionable assistance to users across diverse tasks (e.g., answering questions, solving problems, offering guidance), often operationalized as a core alignment objective in large language models. It is frequently defined through reward modeling, prompt-based specifications, or human/LLM evaluations emphasizing clarity, informativeness, and task completion, though some papers highlight tensions between helpfulness and other attributes like truthfulness or safety (e.g., avoiding overly brief or non-informative replies). While broadly scoped to include medical, instructional, or creative domains, it is sometimes critiqued as a non-capability attribute primarily tuned post-training to align with human preferences rather than intrinsic model competence.
